diagram_math_checks.justification: Given defines n vertices per ring, successive rings shifted by alpha=pi/n. For a fixed adjacent pair of rings, choose the angular origin on the lower ring: lower vertices 2k alpha, upper vertices (2k+1) alpha, modulo 2pi. The left panel has seven vertices and eleven visible edge segments (three lower, two upper, six oblique), producing five consecutive triangular faces. Periodic continuation has n upward and n downward faces, hence 2n per band as step 1.1 states. The two truncated ends are not joined; the panel explicitly represents only part of the band.

For a representative face choose A=(r cos alpha,-r sin alpha,0), B=(r cos alpha,r sin alpha,0), C=(r,0,h). Its base midpoint is M=(r cos alpha,0,0) and Q=(r,0,0) lies vertically below C on the cylinder. MQ has length r(1-cos alpha), QC has length h, and MQ is perpendicular to QC. MC is perpendicular to AB, so MC is the face altitude ell. The right panel explicitly contains all three closing edges MQ, QC, CM and the right-angle mark at Q. All three vertices are filled points, not endpoint rings.

From the local coordinate cross-product definition and the triangle/surface-density suppliers read, B-A=(0,2r sin alpha,0) and C-A=(s,r sin alpha,h), so their cross product is (2r h sin alpha,0,-2r s sin alpha). One face has area r sin alpha sqrt(h^2+s^2). Multiplying by 2nm and substituting h=H/m, s=r(1-cos alpha) gives exactly step 1.1. The drawing asserts ell^2=h^2+s^2; its axes are radial and vertical, with no claim of isometric angular unfolding.

Executed coordinate cross-product versus base-altitude area calculations for r=2,H=3,m=n^3 and n=2,3,6,20. Both expressions respectively gave 4.069705149024926, 1.742709682373124, 0.26830890957822967, 0.007704764764251779; absolute differences were zero at JavaScript precision. The symbolic calculation above supplies the general justification.

All original mathematical and proof bytes remain intact. Remarks explicitly state schematic panels with different scales and independence of the proof/limits. No maps or commutative relations are asserted by this geometric illustration.
